plumbing.summary: Everything passed: gofmt, go vet, the tests of every package the change touches, and every acceptance test.
plumbing.review:
I couldn't run anything (my tools are read-only), so the pass results come from tests.txt; everything else comes from reading the code. The change is close, but one gap against the plan's summary needs fixing before it merges. A large plan's proposal post gets silently cut off, ratify command included, while the hash still pins the whole plan.

## 1. Does what the summary says, and nothing more

- **Scope is right.** Only the plan's seven files are touched. Everything the summary lists is there:
  - `IssuePlan`, `MaxIssues`, the hash over name, summary and each title and body in order, and `ReadIssues`: `repo/internal/formalize/issueplan.go:26-100`, `:175-187`.
  - `Request.PRD` is handled first: `repo/internal/formalize/agent.go:139-141`.
  - The PRD path overrides the issue's own `Kind:`, `Project:` and `Code:` lines: `repo/internal/factory/factory.go:643-651`, `:656`, `:674`, `:691`.
  - A ratified plan skips the build: `factory.go:465`.
  - Ratify goes to `ratifyIssuePlan`: `factory.go:1001-1003`.
- **Two small extras** fit within "a title" and "a clean directory": titles must be one line (`issueplan.go:77-78`), and `.git` is rejected (`:163`).
- **Must fix: the post can be cut off.** The summary says the post shows every issue's whole body with the ratify command.
  - `issuePlanComment` does include everything (`repo/internal/factory/issueplan.go:62-72`).
  - But `post` trims the end off any comment over 60,000 characters (`repo/internal/factory/comments.go:33-48`). The ratify line is at the end, so it goes first.
  - The hidden marker at the end of the post is kept whole, so the hash still pins text the person can't see.
  - Nothing limits a plan's size: `Validate` checks only the issue count and each issue's shape (`formalize/issueplan.go:56-71`). The prompt asks for bodies that stand on their own (`:296`).
  - The marker holds the plan a second time (compressed), so by my estimate a 10-issue plan hits the limit at roughly 4,000 characters per issue.
- **Edge case (recommended):** `isPRD` looks for any writer's `/invariant plan` in the thread (`factory/issueplan.go:22`), including one the factory turned down with "I'm already working on this issue." (`factory.go:501`).
  - Example: a writer says it while a failed pull request is open. The pull request is later closed, and a `/invariant revise` then silently drafts a plan of issues. The issue can never go back to statements.

## 2. The acceptance tests

- **The tests weren't touched.** Both test files match the plan's `sources`.
- **They test the real code, with no special cases.**
  - The test repository is `o/r` (`repo/internal/factory/factory_test.go:40`). Without `isPRD`, the `Kind: plumbing` body would have been answered as unsupported (`factory.go:656-660`). So "whatever the issue's own Kind: line says" is really tested.
  - Forks, answers and revisions go through the existing `choose` and `Revise` code.
  - The second poll in the ratify test confirms nothing is built or posted twice.
- **One gap:** `issuesTool` (`repo/cmd/invariant/main.go:457-490`) has no test. It's a thin wrapper over `ReadIssues`.

## 3. Checks, network, host, secrets

- **The issue protocol is enforced.** Drafts go through `draftStep`.
  - The new `/invariant plan` command drafts only from states where the protocol's existing Solve or Revise steps allow a draft (`repo/factory/protocol/protocol/protocol.go:224`, `:265`).
  - Ratifying goes through `ratifyStep` and `allowed` (`factory/issueplan.go:41-44`), and the plan is re-hashed against the proposal first (`:34-36`).
- **The recovery check is accurate.** `ratifying(true)` (`:47`) claims the ratification was pushed. A ratify's only prerequisite is that push (`repo/factory/recovery/recovery/recovery.go:124`), and a plan has nothing to push. The lease check still applies.
- **No new network or host access.** `mcp -issues` only reads two files in the workspace (`main.go:312-319`). The planning agent gets the same export of the base branch that plumbing already gets. The dashboard's `/act` endpoint allows only exact command lines (`repo/internal/dashboard/act.go:222-248`), so the new verb doesn't widen it.
- **An existing weakness gets wider (recommended fix):** issue bodies are shown as rendered Markdown (`factory/issueplan.go:63`, `:91-93`).
  - An HTML comment in a body is invisible to the ratifier, yet pinned by the hash, and in the second half it would be opened verbatim as part of the issue.
  - A `<!-- invariant:… -->` inside a body would be read as the post's hidden marker, because `DecodeMarker` takes the first match (`repo/internal/factory/thread.go:183`).
  - Agent text already sits ahead of the marker in other posts, but these bodies are the largest such channel yet. Rejecting `<!--` in `Validate` closes both for plans.
- **Minor:** if the watcher stops after the ratified post but before the labels are cleared (`factory/issueplan.go:51`, `factory.go:1789-1794`), the "awaiting ratification" label stays. Nothing clears it later (`factory.go:465`).

## 4. Reads like the code around it

It mostly does. `PlanIssues` and `IssuesPrompt` closely mirror `Plan` and `PlanPrompt`, and the D-0105 citation for the 10-issue limit is correct. Small points:

- `issueCount` re-implements `plural` (`repo/internal/factory/numbers.go:89`).
- `blockquote` is the existing `quote` without its line limit (`comments.go:468`). That's justified by "whole body", but worth a comment saying so.
- `issueLines` claims to read lines "as the factory reads them" (`formalize/issueplan.go:102-104`), but it doesn't strip `/` from a `Project:` value the way `projectLine` does (`factory.go:839`). Being stricter is harmless; the comment is inaccurate.
- The `KindRatified` comment edit reads awkwardly next to its neighbors (`thread.go:89`).
- The error text has a double "which" (`formalize/issueplan.go:97` with `:166`).
- When a failed pull request is still open, turning down `/invariant plan` just says "I'm already working on this issue." `Revise` says what to do instead (`factory.go:506-509`).

**Follow-ups outside this plan's files:**
- The dashboard shows a plan of issues as "proposed 0 statements, checked by TLC" (`repo/internal/dashboard/issues.go:411-420`).
- Clearing the labels drops a ratified plan from the list of issues the factory takes (`thread.go:48-55`), so the dashboard stops listing it.
- The stuck post says "statements" when a plan fails (`comments.go:287`).
- Unlike plumbing, drafting a plan isn't limited to Invariant's own repository (`repo/internal/factory/plumbing.go:40`). Yet the prompt steers toward `Kind: plumbing` issues, which the factory turns down on other repositories.

VERDICT: changes needed — cap a plan of issues' total text in `IssuePlan.Validate` (and state the cap in `IssuesPrompt`) so its proposal post can never exceed the comment limit, where `post()` cuts off the bodies and the ratify command while the hash still pins the whole plan.

usage.summary:
All seven acceptance tests pass, and so do gofmt, `go vet` and the tests of every package I touched. That took 1 of the 6 test runs.

**What changed**
- **`internal/formalize/issueplan.go` (new):** the plan of issues itself.
  - `IssuePlan` and `PlannedIssue`, with `MaxIssues = 10`.
  - `Hash`: a sha256 over the name, the summary, and each title and body, in order.
  - `Validate` checks the plan's rules, `ReadIssues` reads `issues.json`, and `Formalizer.PlanIssues` runs the planning agent, with its prompt.
  - In the other formalize files: `Request.PRD` sends `Formalize` to the planner, and the result comes back as `Proposal.IssuePlan`.
- **`cmd/invariant/main.go`:** `invariant mcp -issues` serves the agent's `check` tool.
- **Factory:**
  - `/invariant plan` is a new command (`thread.go`).
  - Once a writer has commented it, every draft for that issue is a plan of issues, whatever its Kind:, Project: or Code: lines say.
  - A plan gets its own proposal post, showing the name and each issue's title and whole body, quoted.
  - Ratifying it is checked against the protocol, as any proposal is. It posts once and builds nothing, and later polls leave the ratified plan alone.

**Calls the plan didn't settle**
- **What `/invariant plan` does in each state:** it drafts afresh, with no earlier answers or draft, wherever `solve` or `revise` could draft. Otherwise it replies "I'm already working on this issue." It only counts in a comment, not in the issue's body the way `/invariant solve` does. Once a writer has asked, a later `solve` or `revise` also drafts a plan.
- **Validation:** it reads Kind:, Project: and Code: lines the way the factory will read them. On top of the plan's rules, it also rejects:
  - any `/invariant <word>` line outside code blocks, whatever the word, so a command added later can't slip into a plan;
  - a title longer than one line;
  - a Project: under `.git/`.

  A trailing slash on the Project: directory is allowed. Unknown fields in `issues.json` are refused, as they are in `plan.json`.
- **Labels after ratification:** ratifying clears the issue's status label. That's accurate, because nothing is in progress, but the dashboard and `invariant ledger` find issues by their labels, so a ratified plan drops out of both. The dashboard also describes a plan proposal as "proposed 0 statements". Both need changes to files outside this plan.
- **Recovery check:** the ratified post passes the recovery rules as a ratification that's already pushed. There's nothing to push, so everything that comes before the post is done.
- **Decisions not recorded:** AGENTS.md says calls like these go on record with `invariant decisions decide`. I was told not to touch `decisions/` and have no shell, so none of them are recorded yet. You may want them logged.
